grades.quote: the interleaving of the threads’ execution needs to be at the granularity of complete operations, such as selling a ticket or auditing the cash drawer.
grades.reason: Explains the general cause of this kind of bug: a race occurs when threads' operations on shared data are interleaved in the middle of an operation instead of at the granularity of complete operations. It also gives the fix, mutual exclusion with locks. It uses a ticket/cash example rather than a single shared counter's lost update, so it only covers part of the question.

grades.quote: the bottom line for programmers is still that synchronization should be used to avoid races in the first place; trying to understand the race behavior is a losing battle.
grades.reason: Notes that unsynchronized threads can behave in odd ways and that synchronization should be used to avoid races. It also mentions atomic read-and-update instructions such as atomic increment. It never explains why a shared counter ends up too small, so it only helps a little.
Covers recursive mutex behavior in POSIX. It does not address lost updates to a shared counter.
Covers RISC-V cycle and instret hardware counter behavior under privilege mode filtering. It has nothing to do with software threads incrementing a shared counter.
